title: Fideuram scam using a fake WhatsApp and an AI-engineered voice: €36 million vanished.
key_facts: Former Fideuram president Paolo Molesini (Fideuram is owned by Intesa) was the victim of a scam using a fake WhatsApp message and an AI-manipulated phone call, Corriere della Sera reported on 3 Oct 2026 (as relayed by L'Unione Sarda).
The scam dates from last February (2026): a WhatsApp message appeared to come from Carlo Messina of parent company Banca Intesa, urging a series of transfers through Fideuram's treasury.
A second fake contact appeared to be a lawyer Molesini knows, Paolo Nastasi of A&O Shearman Italia, who knew nothing about it; his voice was copied with AI tools.
Transfers of about 95 million euros were sent, mostly to China and Hong Kong (the article also names Portugal).

Fideuram raised the alarm and used international bank cooperation to recover a large portion; over 40 million euros were frozen in China and 13 million in a Portuguese bank (seizure order from last May).

At least 36 million euros were still missing, having vanished into cryptocurrencies; Milan prosecutors are pursuing the gang through letters rogatory (formal requests to foreign authorities) and at least one suspect, possibly a false identity, is registered.
quote_evidence: Former Fideuram president Paolo Molesini was the victim of a €36 million scam involving a fake WhatsApp message and a phone call manipulated with artificial intelligence.
However, the alarm was raised, and Fideuram activated its international interbank collaboration systems, allowing the recovery of a large portion of the loot.
At least €36 million was still missing, having vanished into cryptocurrencies.
why_it_matters_hint: A fake message plus a copied voice moved tens of millions of euros out of a major bank's treasury.
event_date: February 2026 (exact day not given); first reported 3 Oct 2026
notes: Second-hand report of Corriere della Sera's story; no court finding. The article's figures are not fully consistent (36 million euros missing in the headline and text, about 95 million sent, 40 million frozen in China, 13 million in Portugal) and the victim's name is spelled 'Moresini' once. Event is months old, first reported now.
